title: Activation Balancer INT8 pipeline and runtime adapter for KV-cache friendly serving
creator: Maya Patel
description: Goal: deliver an activation-aware INT8 calibration pipeline and lightweight runtime adapter that (1) produces per-workload scaling profiles compatible with our existing model catalog, (2) preserves KV-cache correctness and decoding determinism for long-sequence chat workloads, and (3) plugs into the runtime kernel selector with minimal codegen churn. This ticket implements the 'activation balancer' flow (smooth-style scaling without changing model weights) end-to-end: offline profile generator, compact profile artifact format, validation harness, runtime shim for fused-attention kernels, and an automated canary/rollback policy for hosted and Dedicated deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Profile generator produces compact profile artifacts (<200KB) for 7B and 13B base/residual models
End-to-end throughput regression vs FP16 baseline < 10% on p4d when enabling INT8 profiles
Token-level output drift measured by evaluation harness < 0.5% for standard prompt-suite and <1.0% for adversarial prompts
KV-cache preserved: identical cached key/value shapes and numerical tolerances within +/- 1e-3 after scaling
Runtime adapter exposes feature flag and automatic fallback to FP16 when unsupported kernel chosen
Canary rollout pipeline that supports 1% incremental traffic and automated rollback on quality regression
notes_and_decisions: We will store per-layer scaling factors as quantized int16 values in a compact protobuf to avoid runtime parsing cost.
Decided to implement two calibration modes: 'fast' (single pass, lower compute) and 'robust' (multi-batch, outlier clipping). Default for hosted is 'robust'.
Runtime will implement adapter that rewrites attention fused-kernel index mapping to apply scale compensation during KV packing to avoid cache invalidation.
To minimize operator surface, we will not alter model ONNX weights; scaling is applied only at runtime and in precomputed profiles.
Performance target relaxed from 5% to 10% regression to avoid risky kernel fusion changes before runtime-1.20.
Will add an end-to-end CI job that runs calibration -> runtime serve -> evaluation on small prompt suite nightly.
Follow-up ticket planned for per-customer profile pinning and audit logging (ENG-XXXXX).

implementation_plan: Phase 1: Spec profile format, add generator to calibration harness, integrate robust clipping (2 days)
Phase 2: Implement runtime adapter for fused attention pack/unpack and KV scale compensation (4 days)
Phase 3: Validation: accuracy harness + regression testing across small prompt suites and adversarial set (3 days)
Phase 4: Canary rollout config, monitoring dashboards, automated rollback on drift thresholds (2 days)
Phase 5: Docs and SDK example: how to opt-in and pin profiles (1 day)
risks: Kernel rewrite could cause subtle numerical differences for long-context decoding: mitigated by KV-preserving shim and regression harness
Profile artifacts may blow up in size if per-channel scaling on large FFNs is used; fallback to per-layer quantization if >300KB
Customer regressions for highly tuned prompt templates: we will run per-customer canaries before global rollout
